text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah on Sunday received a message from Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.
- Summer lull expected at Kuwait's property market, specialised firm says.

- Kuwait's planned privatisation of 30 fuel stations requires approval by Ministry of Trade and Industry, Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi says. Kuwait has announced plans to sell 30 of about 80 state-owned petrol stations to the private sector under a wide-ranging privatisation programme.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange index falls 49.2 points to 2,381.3 amid talk of a Central Bank's decision to bar margin loans which was announced after the end of the trade session.

- Ministry of Trade and Industry completes study on establishing a new mobile telecommunications firm. Currently Mobile Telecommunications Co (MTC) is the sole provider of mobile telephone and pager services.
- Kuwait on Sunday hailed Gulf Arab states' for calling Baghdad to release about 600 Kuwaitis believed to be detained in Iraq since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
